messages:
support_lead: FYI: getting a big spike of 5xx from hosted inference API starting ~2026-03-15T09:42Z. Multiple customers reporting failed requests and increased latencies. Early traces show control-plane dependencies returning 5xx (auth/session, routing-policy, and config DB timeouts).

maya: which endpoints are failing most often? any customer examples we can repro with?

support_lead: customers report failures across text-gen and embeddings endpoints. Example from customer request-id: req_0a9f3b (attached) — they see a chain of errors: auth validate -> config DB -> routing policy fetch -> 502/503.

eng_oncall: looking at edge logs, pattern is: auth-service calls config-db for session/tenant config, that call is timing out and auth-service returns 500 which propagates as 502 at gateway. snippet:```
[09:42:17] auth-service ERROR auth/validate.go:142 tenant=acme timeout getting session from config-db: context deadline exceeded
[09:42:17] gateway WARN  proxy.go:88 upstream returned 502 for req=req_0a9f3b
[09:42:17] routing-service ERROR route/fetch.go:67 failed to load policy: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection timed out
```

db_admin: config-db metrics show connection_pool_wait_count spiking and p95 acquire latency > 5s. We have max_connections=250 on the primary, and fatigue started at ~09:40Z. Seeing a few slow queries from auth-service:```
SELECT id, tenant_id, session_expires FROM sessions WHERE token = $1; -- 340ms
SELECT policy_blob FROM routing_policies WHERE tenant_id = $1 FOR UPDATE; -- 2.1s (locks)
```

platform_sre: confirmed — routing-service is fanouting policy lookups to config-db for every auth validation during short TTL expiry. Recent change in routing-policy client removed local caching (v2.3.1), deployed as canary yesterday. Rolling that out seems to coincide with spike.

maya: so two contributors: removed cache + DB pool saturation -> auth times out -> gateway 5xx. Any mitigation we can do right now?

platform_sre: immediate mitigations applied: 1) rolled back routing-policy client to v2.3.0 for the canary hosts (deploy-bot confirmed). 2) increased config-db max_connections by +100 on primaries and added one read-replica to absorb fanout. 3) enabled fallback in auth-service to treat config-db timeouts as soft-fail and use last-known policy for 30s.

deploy-bot: rollback completed for routing-policy-canary at 09:55:12Z — rollout id 5632.

routing-bot: routing-policy service autoscale triggered +2 replicas at 09:56Z due to CPU and latency alerts.

eng_oncall: after mitigations we see error rate drop ~85% in 10m. Current trend: 5xx rate back to baseline but still some residual p50 auth latency at 300ms.

support_lead: customers notified (NDA customers and paid seats) — support sent templated message and created tickets for top 6 impacted customers.

maya: repro steps for engineering to run locally:```
# simulate high QPS with expired-cache behavior
for i in $(seq 1 1000); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer expired-token" \"https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/generate\" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' &
done
# watch auth-service logs and config-db pool stats
```

db_admin: to avoid recurrence: recommending: 1) restore routing client caching or add a very small in-process cache (TTL 30s) 2) increase DB connection pool and set backpressure on auth-service when DB queue length exceeds threshold 3) add circuit breaker so routing-service falls back to cached policy on repeated DB timeouts.

platform_sre: created a short-term alert: config-db acquire_wait_count > 500 for 2m triggers paging. Created ticket INFRA-1123 for permanent fix (add connection pooling proxy and client-side caching).

eng_oncall: collecting traces and span ids, attaching to INFRA-1123 and support tickets. Will follow up with a postmortem template once we stabilise.

support_lead: Postmortem owners: eng_oncall, db_admin, platform_sre. SLA impact: we estimate ~12k requests affected over 18 minutes for hosted API (rough calc from ingest metrics).

maya: any lingering customer action items? follow-up scheduled at 15:00UTC to share RCA and timeline.

support_lead: thanks all — marking thread resolved for now, will reopen if error rate climbs again. :white_check_mark:
